title: People Ops 20 Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
reviewers: Marcus Lee, Sofia Ramirez, Daniel O'Connor
body:
Purpose:
This document codifies Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for recruiting, candidate evaluation, new-hire onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager best-practices. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers joining the company.

Scope:
Covers full-time and long-term contractor hiring, the 90-day onboarding program, quarterly and annual performance processes, probation rules, and manager responsibilities for hiring and career development. This does NOT replace employment contracts or legal policy documents maintained by Finance & Legal.

Contents:
1) Hiring process overview
2) Interviewer responsibilities & evaluation rubric
3) Offer approval & background checks
4) Onboarding: pre-boarding, week 1, 30-60-90 plan
5) Performance & feedback cycles
6) Manager guide and recommended 1:1 cadence
7) People policies & SLAs for People Ops
8) Ownership, escalation, and useful links

1) Hiring process overview
- Goals and SLA targets (people-ops metrics):
  - Median time-to-offer target: 35 days (pipeline open -> verbal offer).
  - Median time-to-fill target: 45 days (requisition approved -> start date).
  - Offer acceptance rate target: >= 70%.
  - New-hire onboarding completion: 90% complete required trainings within 7 days.

- Standard steps (numbered procedure):
  1. Requisition creation: Manager completes a Requisition Form in Greenhouse with role, band, justification, and hiring committee. People Ops assigns a recruiter and posts the role.
  2. Sourcing and screening: Recruiter sources candidates; initial phone screen or take-home may be used depending on role.
  3. Interview loop: Hiring committee runs the interview loop (see section 2). Interviewers submit evaluations within 48 hours.
  4. Debrief and calibration: Hiring manager leads a debrief within 24 hours of final interview to review rubric scores and evidence.
  5. Offer approval: Manager prepares Offer Packet; compensation above band or equity > standard grant requires Director/VP approval.
  6. Background checks & references: Conditional offer issued; background check initiated.
  7. Onboarding and start: People Ops schedules pre-boarding and start activities.

- Requisition approvals and thresholds:
  - Any offer with base pay > 120% of band midpoint requires VP People approval.
  - Hiring for Manager-level roles and above requires an org leadership hiring sign-off.

2) Interviewer responsibilities & evaluation rubric
- Panel size and composition:
  - Typical panel: 3-4 interviewers (technical peer, cross-functional partner, manager, and optional recruiter/PM).
  - At least one interviewer must be a trained interviewer (completed Redwood interviewer training).

- Interview structure guidelines (30/60/90 minute formats):
  - Present role context and expectations (5 minutes).
  - Structured questions aligned to rubric (20-40 minutes).
  - Candidate questions and wrap-up (5-15 minutes).

- Evaluation rubric (submit in Greenhouse):
  - Core dimensions: Technical skills, Problem solving, Product judgment (if applicable), Communication & collaboration, Culture add & values alignment.
  - Scoring: 1 (insufficient) - 2 (below expectations) - 3 (meets expectations) - 4 (exceeds) - 5 (outstanding).
  - Hiring threshold: Average score >= 3.2 and no score of 1 in a critical dimension for advancement to offer.

- Interviewer obligations:
  - Submit written notes and rubric within 48 hours.
  - Disclose any conflicts of interest to the recruiter immediately.
  - Be prompt: notify recruiter at least 24 hours in advance if cancelling.

- Common pitfalls and calibration tips:
  - Avoid relying solely on take-home assignments; weigh the assignment against live problem-solving and communication evidence.
  - Use evidence-based language in notes ("candidate designed X that handled Y because...") rather than absolute judgments.

3) Offer approval & background checks
- Offer packet contents:
  - Role, level/band, base salary, equity grant, sign-on bonus (if applicable), start date, manager, office/remote status, relocation details (if any).
  - Standard benefits summary and link to the benefits enrollment portal.

- Approval workflow:
  1. Manager prepares Offer Packet in Greenhouse.
  2. Recruiter reviews for comp-band alignment and budget.
  3. Director/VP approval if above thresholds (see section 1).
  4. People Ops issues conditional offer.

- Background checks and references:
  - Vendor: Redwood uses Sterling for employment/education background checks (standard package). Certain regulated roles require extended checks and security clearances - People Ops will advise.
  - Reference checks: At least two professional references collected for senior roles (L4+); recruiter completes reference template.

4) Onboarding: pre-boarding, week 1, 30-60-90 plan
- Pre-boarding checklist (to be completed by People Ops and hiring manager prior to start date):
  - New-hire paperwork sent (Rippling).
  - IT provisioning request filed (Okta, laptop order, Slack, email alias).
  - First-week calendar blocked: orientation, team intro, role deep-dive, security & compliance training.
  - Assign buddy and onboarding mentor.

- Week 1 objectives:
  - Complete mandatory trainings: security, code of conduct, data handling (target: within 7 days).
  - Meet core collaborators: manager 1:1, two cross-functional peers, and buddy.
  - Environment setup: dev environment for engineering hires, access to key dashboards for product/ops hires.

- 30-60-90 day plan (example milestones):
  - Day 30: Understand tech stack or product area; deliver first small-ticket contribution or onboarding project.
  - Day 60: Own a feature or process with reduced supervision; participate in roadmap discussions.
  - Day 90: Fully ramped on core responsibilities; manager completes probation review.

- Onboarding metrics and acceptance criteria:
  - Role readiness score: manager rates new-hire on a 1-5 ramp readiness scale at day 30/60/90. Target: >=3 at day 60 and >=4 at day 90.
  - Training completion: 100% completion of required trainings by day 30.

- New-hire checklist table (text table):
  - IT Provisioning: "Okta / laptop / email alias" - Owner: IT - Due: before start
  - Orientation & HR paperwork: "Rippling workflows" - Owner: People Ops - Due: day 1
  - Role onboarding doc: "Team onboarding README + 30-60-90" - Owner: Manager - Due: day 1
  - Buddy assignment: "Buddy assigned" - Owner: Manager - Due: day 1

5) Performance & feedback cycles
- Performance cycles and cadence:
  - Continuous feedback encouraged; managers should document substantive feedback in Lattice (or approved tool).
  - Formal cycles: Quarterly check-ins and an annual review cycle (calendar: mid-year in June, annual in December).
  - Probation review at day 90 for new hires.

- Goal setting and calibration:
  - Each employee sets 3-5 team-aligned objectives (OKRs or SMART goals) each cycle.
  - Managers submit calibration summaries to People Ops during calibration windows.

- Review mechanics and ratings:
  - Rating scale: 1 (Needs improvement), 2 (Meets expectations), 3 (Exceeds expectations), 4 (Outstanding) - numeric mapping used for comp review.
  - Ratings require evidence: at least three documented examples supporting a rating change.
  - Calibration panel: consists of manager peers, HRBP, and a department leader; panel reviews distributions and outliers.

- Promotion & compensation timing:
  - Promos considered outside formal cycle require manager and director justification and People Ops approval.
  - Compensation adjustments tied to performance reviews and budget windows (People Ops publishes budget calendar annually).

- Handling performance concerns:
  - Informal coaching: documented 1:1 notes and clear expectations.
  - Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): used when coaching does not yield sustained improvement. PIP duration typically 60-90 days; HRBP and Manager jointly own the process.

6) Manager guide and recommended 1:1 cadence
- 1:1 cadence recommendations:
  - New manager: weekly 1:1s for first 3 months.
  - Individual contributors: 1:1 every 1-2 weeks depending on role.
  - Managers should maintain 1:1 notes and action items; share progress in the next meeting.

- Hiring best practices for managers:
  - Define success criteria and non-negotiables before opening a req.
  - Use structured interviews and keep panels diverse (skill-wise and demographically).
  - Provide timely feedback to candidates (target: within 3 business days of final interview).

- Career development and growth conversations:
  - Document career conversations at least quarterly.
  - Provide concrete development plans with skills, stretch projects, and mentoring.

- Offboarding / Role transitions:
  - Manager initiates role transition plan at least 30 days prior to departure when possible.
  - Knowledge transfer docs and runbooks required for ICs owning critical systems.

7) People policies & SLAs for People Ops
- Key policies (summary):
  - Probation period: 90 days for full-time hires.
  - Paid time off: unlimited vacation with manager approval and recommended guideline of 3-4 weeks/year for planning.
  - Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 6 weeks secondary (as of policy published date).
  - Remote & hybrid policy: employees are assigned a default work model on offer; exceptions handled via manager/People Ops.
  - Confidentiality & data handling: all employees must complete mandatory data handling training during week 1.

- People Ops service-level agreements (internal):
  - Recruiter initial reach-out to hiring manager: within 3 business days of requisition approval.
  - Offer issuance after final approval: target within 48 hours.
  - IT provisioning for standard laptops: ship within 7 business days of start date.

8) Ownership, escalation, and useful links
- Primary owners:
  - Global Head of People Ops: Sofia Ramirez - high-level policy, escalations.
  - Recruiting lead: Marcus Lee - sourcing, ATS workflows.
  - HRBP for Eng & Product: Daniel O'Connor - performance programs and calibration.

- Escalation matrix:
  1. Hiring manager -> Recruiter
  2. Recruiter -> Recruiting Lead (Marcus Lee)
  3. Recruiting Lead -> Head of People Ops (Sofia Ramirez)

Appendix: Example interview questions by dimension (text list)
- Technical: "Describe a time you diagnosed a production performance incident. What steps did you take and what was the outcome?"
- Problem solving: "Given X data, how would you prioritize next steps? Walk me through your assumptions."
- Communication: "Explain a complex technical decision to a non-technical stakeholder."
- Culture/values: "Tell us about a time you gave or received difficult feedback. What did you learn?"

Contact for questions:

- recruiting@redwoodai.com (sourcing/reqs)

Document notes: This is a living document. Managers and People Ops partners should treat the SLAs and numerical targets as operational goals, updated quarterly based on capacity and hiring needs. For legal policy and benefits authoritative source, refer to Finance & Legal documentation.
